title: Families
examples: What are some different types of families?
How do roles change in a modern family?
Can you give an example of a family that is different from the traditional one?

explain.say: Today we are looking at how families are different.
Some families have two parents and children living together.
Some families might have grandparents living with them too.
Roles in a family can change a lot over time.
Families are always changing because of laws and culture.

items: When: Past: Fewer legal rights for women
When: Present: More legal rights for all genders

draw.text: Change: Laws and society affect families.

explain.say: In real life, think about how families support each other.

faq.q: What is the difference between a nuclear and an extended family?
faq.a: A nuclear family usually means parents and children only. An extended family includes other relatives like grandparents or aunts and uncles living together.
asks: What is the difference between these family structures?

faq.q: Do roles have to stay the same in a family?
faq.a: No, roles are flexible and change as people grow up or as society changes. For example, both parents might work now.
asks: Are roles fixed in a family?

faq.q: Does culture affect what a family looks like?
faq.a: Yes, culture strongly influences family structure and roles. Different cultures have different accepted norms for family life.
asks: Are all families the same across the world?

faq.q: What causes families to change over time?
faq.a: Major social, legal, and economic changes cause families to adapt. New laws or jobs can change who does what.

faq.q: Is it okay for my family to be different from my friends' families?
faq.a: Absolutely. The important thing is that the family provides support and care for its members. Diversity is normal.
asks: Is my family normal if it looks different?

facts: Family structures are diverse across global cultures.
Roles within a family can be shared between all members.
Societal laws and economic changes often prompt family adjustments.
Support networks are vital for the well-being of all family members.

quiz.say: A family consisting of parents and children living together is called a:
quiz.why: This describes the basic unit of two parents and their children.

wrong.0: This is a general term describing variety, not a specific structure.
wrong.1: This describes a time period, not the structure itself.
wrong.3: This term includes more relatives like grandparents.

quiz.say: If both parents work outside the home, this shows a change in:
quiz.why: Roles refer to the expected duties, which can change over time.

wrong.0: Structure refers to who lives together, not what they do.
wrong.1: Laws are the cause, but 'roles' is what is changing in the family unit.
wrong.3: Diversity refers to the variety of structures, not just the roles.

quiz.say: A family that includes grandparents, parents, and children is best described as:
quiz.why: The inclusion of multiple generations defines an extended family.

wrong.0: This is too general and does not describe the specific grouping of people.
wrong.3: While it is diverse, 'extended family' is the specific term for this grouping.
